facts.statement: The genus is known from complete skeletons collected by fossil hunter Thomas Hawkins in Somerset, England, in the early 1830s.
facts.quote: Thalassiodracon hawkinsii is known from a number of complete skeletons (lectotype: NHMUK PV OR 2018) acquired by the fossil collector Thomas Hawkins in Somerset, England during the early 1830s, before 1834.

facts.statement: Richard Owen named the species Plesiosaurus hawkinsii in 1838, and Storrs and Taylor established the genus Thalassiodracon in 1996.
facts.quote: It was named as Plesiosaurus Hawkinsii in 1838 by Richard Owen and it was made the type species of the genus Thalassiodracon in 1996 by Storrs & Taylor.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon was a small plesiosaur measuring approximately 1.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: It measured approximately 1.5 m long.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon had a relatively short neck with between 27 and 31 cervical vertebrae, fewer than the 35 to 37 found in Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: The neck of Thalassiodracon was slightly shorter than that of subsequent plesiosaurs. The cervical vertebrae were between 27 and 31, while those of Plesiosaurus were 35 - 37.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon possessed an unusually short skull equipped with long teeth.
facts.quote: The skull was unusually short and equipped with long teeth.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon had enlarged orbits with large, flat scleral rings, theorized to help its eyes adapt to low-light underwater environments.
facts.quote: The orbits of the skull were enlarged, containing likewise large, flat scleral rings. These rings are theorized to help the eyes of the creature to be well adjusted for a low-light environment found in its habitat.

facts.statement: Features such as elongated staples and fused exoccipital bones suggest that Thalassiodracon had adaptations for underwater hearing.
facts.quote: Other features like elongated staples and fused exoccipital bones seem to suggest adapted underwater hearing.

facts.statement: In adulthood, Thalassiodracon had forelimbs that were shorter than its hindlimbs.
facts.quote: In adulthood, the forelimbs of Thalassiodracon hawkinsii are shorter than its hindlimbs.

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that Thalassiodracon was a pursuit predator that used speed and strength to hunt prey, based on its limb proportions.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurs with this characteristic are speculated to be pursuit predators, using speed and strength to hunt down their prey.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon was likely warm-blooded with a high metabolism, allowing for an active lifestyle unlike modern reptiles.
facts.quote: Unlike the reptiles of today, Thalassiodracon hawkinsii and other plesiosaurs were warm-blooded with a high metabolism, enabling them to have an active lifestyle.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon had paddle-like legs for swimming and possessed a shortened tail, a trait distinguishing it from earlier ancestors.
facts.quote: Like all plesiosaurs, this animal had legs like paddles for swimming in the sea. But, separating them from earlier ancestors, Thalassiodracon and following members also had shortened tails.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon is believed to have been viviparous, giving birth to live young.
facts.quote: Like other plesiosaurs, Thalassiodracon hawkinsii is believed to have been viviparous, meaning it gave birth to live young.

facts.statement: The presence of dinosaur and pterosaur bones in plesiosaur remains suggests that Thalassiodracon may have occasionally preyed on these animals.
facts.quote: With the bones of dinosaurs and pterosaurs being found in plesiosaur remains, these animals are also possibilities for their diets.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon is considered one of the oldest plesiosaur representatives and may be ancestral to the superfamily Pliosauroidea.
facts.quote: This animal is considered one of the oldest representatives of the group of plesiosaurs, perhaps ancestral to the superfamily of Pliosauroidea (short-necked plesiosaurs).

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon lived in Europe from the Late Triassic to the Early Jurassic, approximately 201.6 to 196.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Thalassiodracon was a small plesiosaur in the Late Triassic (Rhaetian) to the Early Jurassic (Hettangian) of Europe (age range: 201.6 to 196.5 million years ago).

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon measured between 1.5 and 2 meters long and had a skull that was proportionally larger than that of Plesiosaurus, accounting for 1/10 of its total body length.
facts.quote: Este reptil marino medía entre 1.5–2 metros de largo, y tenía un cuello relativamente alargado pero con un cráneo proporcionalmente más grande que el de Plesiosaurus, ya que corresponde a 1/10 de la longitud corporal total.

facts.statement: The skull of Thalassiodracon featured elongated teeth and very large eye orbits containing sclerotic rings.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, el cráneo contaba con dientes alargados. Las órbitas oculares eran muy grandes, con anillos escleróticos.

facts.statement: CT scans and specimen examinations revealed that Thalassiodracon had a dorsal ridge on the premaxilla, a bulbous squamosal, four premaxillary teeth, and heterodont maxillary dentition.
facts.quote: Una tomografía computarizada de un cráneo excepcionalmente preservado, y el examen de otros especímenes (Benson et al., 2011) permitió obtener nuevos datos anatómicos. Thalassiodracon tenía una cresta dorsal en el medio del premaxilar, un escamosal bulboso, cuatro dientes premaxilares, y una dentadura maxilar heterodonta.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon lived in Europe from the Late Triassic (Rhaetian) to the Early Jurassic (Hettangian), between 201.6 and 196.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Vivió entre finales del Triásico (época del Rhaetiense) a inicios del Jurásico (Hettangiense) de Europa, entre hace 201.6 a 196.5 millones de años.

facts.statement: Thalassiodracon is considered one of the oldest plesiosaur representatives and may be ancestral to the superfamily Pliosauroidea, which includes short-necked plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Este animal se considera como uno de los más antiguos representantes del grupo de los plesiosaurios, quizás siendo ancestral con respecto a la superfamilia Pliosauroidea (que incluye plesiosaurios de cuello corto).

facts.statement: The fossil record for Thalassiodracon spans from the Hettangian to the Pliensbachian stages, between 201.4 and 184.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Pliensbachian (201.4 to 184.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Thalassiodracon is an extinct genus of short-necked plesiosaur belonging to the family Pliosauridae, found only in the Lower Lias of England.
rejected.quote: Thalassiodracon is an extinct genus of plesiosauroid from the Pliosauridae that was alive during the Late Triassic-Early Jurassic (Rhaetian-Hettangian) and is known exclusively from the Lower Lias of England.
